events.title: William the Conqueror Lands at Pevensey
events.description: Norman forces led by William, Duke of Normandy, landed at Pevensey on the southern coast of England, beginning his invasion to claim the English throne following the death of Edward the Confessor.
events.significance: The landing led to the Battle of Hastings on October 14, 1066, and the Norman Conquest, which transformed English language, law, culture, and aristocracy.

events.title: Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo Reaches California
events.description: Portuguese-born explorer Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo, sailing for Spain, landed at San Diego Bay and claimed the area for the Spanish Crown.
events.significance: Cabrillo's voyage was the first European expedition to explore the coast of present-day California, laying the groundwork for later Spanish colonization of the region.

events.title: Congress Sends the Bill of Rights to the States
events.description: The U.S. Congress voted to send twelve proposed constitutional amendments to the states for ratification, following their approval in the House and Senate.
events.significance: Ten of these amendments were ratified in 1791 and became the Bill of Rights, guaranteeing fundamental freedoms and individual protections in the United States.

events.title: Alexander Fleming Observes Penicillin
events.description: Scottish bacteriologist Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold contaminating a Staphylococcus culture plate at St Mary's Hospital in London had killed the surrounding bacteria.
events.significance: The discovery of penicillin launched the age of antibiotics, revolutionizing medicine and saving millions of lives; Fleming shared the 1945 Nobel Prize for the work.

events.title: Death of Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser
events.description: Gamal Abdel Nasser died of a heart attack in Cairo at age 52, just after brokering a ceasefire between Jordan and the PLO during the Black September crisis.
events.significance: Nasser was a leading figure of Arab nationalism and the Non-Aligned Movement. His death brought Anwar Sadat to power and shifted Egypt's direction in regional and Cold War politics.
